post.caption: Diamond hunters follow chrome diopside. Chrome diopside turns up with kimberlite, the rock that carries diamonds. The name diopside comes from Greek roots meaning double appearance. Chromium gives it a vivid green, nicknamed Siberian emerald. Most gem chrome diopside comes from a deposit in Siberia. Turn one stone and it shows three different greens. Star diopside shows a four rayed star, while star sapphires show six. Tiny needles inside make the star, which shows only on a dome. Because it is fairly soft, it suits earrings and pendants best. Nearly all star diopside comes from India.
